name: À-trous Cross-Bilateral Filtering
definition: A spatial filtering technique applied to gradients (∇θft) and their associated buffers (mt, vt) defined on regular 2D or 3D grids, implemented as a series of à-trous filters to enable fast optimization in inverse rendering.
summary: À-trous cross-bilateral filtering is a spatial technique that smooths gradients for stable inverse rendering optimization by using underlying parameter values rather than noisy gradients to determine edge-stopping weights.
